site.name: fleetatlas
site.summary: FleetAtlas Fictional commercial fleet real-time management SaaS dashboard, used as a UXBench fixture. Pages - `index.html` — Fleet overview map home. Left thin rail nav; top bar with org switcher, view tabs (Map / List / Analytics), search box, alert bell (dropdown shows the 5 most recent on click); status filter strip (All / Running / Idle / Maintenance / Offline / Alert); full-screen SVG city map with 25 vehicles in real-time positions (running vehicles jitter their position every 5 seconds to simulate live updates); clicking a vehicle icon or drawer row → right detail panel slides in; bottom pull-up drawer showing the vehicle list. - Right detail panel (controlled by JS within the map page) — basic info (plate / model / year / VIN / fleet), driver info (with phone / shift / accumulated drive hours), current task (route / location / ETA / remaining miles), historical track SVG (24h / 7d / 30d toggle), fuel and speed sparklines; 4 action buttons (Send command / Contact driver / Maintenance record / Reassign task), with Reassign being a destructive action that has a second-confirmation modal. - `alerts.html` — Alerts center. 4 KPI cards (open / new today / by severity / mean handli

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full fleetatlas system, prioritizing the primary dashboard flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The FleetAtlas dashboard suffers from critical layout and responsiveness issues across both desktop and mobile viewports. On desktop, the sidebar navigation fatally breaks layout on secondary pages by expanding to full width and obscuring core functionality. On mobile, rigid data tables and fixed navigation bars cause severe horizontal overflow, rendering the app highly frustrating to navigate and operate on smaller screens.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full FleetAtlas system, prioritizing the primary dashboard flow, adjacent pages, and mobile responsiveness.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will start on the primary map dashboard, validating view toggles, status filters, and the vehicle details panel. It will specifically test the 'Reassign task' modal for recovery paths. Following this, the agent will traverse the adjacent Alerts, Analytics, and Vehicles pages to evaluate data tables and filtering. Finally, a mobile sweep will assess the small tap target warnings and responsive behavior of sliding panels.
assumptions: Map view icons are clickable elements (SVG/div) that trigger the right detail panel, but clicking rows in the pull-up drawer is a reliable fallback.
Navigation links like Drivers, Routes, Maintenance, and Settings are placeholders (href='#') and do not require deep traversal.
View toggle buttons (Map/List/Analytics) on index.html manipulate the DOM without full page loads.
The Reassign task action involves a secondary confirmation modal.
risk_hotspots: Right detail panel slide-in transition and overlay (z-index issues).
Bottom pull-up drawer behavior and scrollability.
Mobile tap targets for thin rail navigation and view toggle buttons (flagged by prescan).

phases.title: Dashboard Core & Filters
phases.objective: Validate primary dashboard controls, view modes, and status filtering.
key_checks: Toggle between Map, List, and Analytics views using top buttons.
Click various status filter chips (Running, Alert, etc.) and verify map/list updates.
Open the alert bell dropdown to view recent alerts.
Interact with the Org switcher dropdown.
exit_criteria: View modes and status filters have been exercised and state changes observed.

phases.title: Vehicle Detail & Destructive Action
phases.objective: Test the vehicle drill-down flow and the reassign task modal.
key_checks: Open the bottom vehicle list drawer.
Click a vehicle row (or map icon) to open the right detail panel.
Toggle the historical track SVG (24h/7d/30d) inside the detail panel.
Click 'Reassign task' and validate the appearance and functionality (cancel/confirm) of the confirmation modal.
exit_criteria: Detail panel opened successfully, modal invoked and dismissed, and panel closed.

phases.title: Adjacent Pages (Vehicles, Alerts, Analytics)
phases.objective: Explore data-heavy pages for filtering, sorting, and drill-down capabilities.
key_checks: Navigate to vehicles.html, use Fleet/Status dropdowns, and test bulk select checkboxes.
Navigate to alerts.html, use severity/type filters, and click an 'Assign' or 'Details' button.
Navigate to analytics.html and verify the presence of the heatmap and performance table.
exit_criteria: All three pages visited, filters applied, and at least one drill-down action attempted per data table.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness Sweep
phases.objective: Re-run critical flows on mobile viewport to evaluate layout warnings and spatial constraints.
key_checks: Test the left navigation menu (check tap target sizes).
Open the bottom drawer and select a vehicle to trigger the detail panel.
Verify that the detail panel is usable on a small screen and can be dismissed.
exit_criteria: Mobile viewport interactions recorded, specifically testing flagged small tap targets and overlay panels.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit index.html, vehicles.html, alerts.html, and analytics.html.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise map filters, drawer interactions, slide-in panels, modals, and data table filters.
coverage_targets.mobile: Validate the index.html map/drawer/panel flow and navigation tap targets on mobile.

notes: If clicking vehicle icons on the SVG map fails, use the bottom drawer rows to access the detail panel.
Pay special attention to how the right detail panel overlaps or pushes content, especially on mobile.

findings.user_goal: Navigate to and interact with secondary pages like Vehicles, Alerts, and Analytics.
findings.problem: On desktop, the sidebar navigation menu lacks width constraints on secondary pages, stretching across the entire screen (1255px wide).
findings.evidence: Observed on vehicles.html, alerts.html, and analytics.html: The `<aside class="sidebar">` expands to 100% width, visually obscuring the main content area (search, filters, lists) and intercepting all pointer events, causing clicks on elements like 'Details' or 'Assign' to fail.
findings.why_it_matters: Users are completely blocked from viewing data or taking actions on any page other than the main dashboard because the invisible/opaque sidebar overlay prevents interaction with the underlying elements.
findings.suggestion: Apply strict maximum width constraints (e.g., `width: 250px` or `max-width: 20rem`) to the sidebar container on desktop breakpoints to prevent it from overlapping the main content grid.

findings.user_goal: View the list of vehicles on a mobile device.
findings.problem: The Vehicles list page is not responsive and forces a page width of 923px within a 390px mobile viewport.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings flag severe horizontal overflow. The data table containing vehicle details (Plate, Model, Driver, Status, Location) does not reflow, stack, or wrap, requiring the user to scroll horizontally to see core information and action buttons.
findings.why_it_matters: Forcing two-dimensional scrolling (vertical and horizontal) on mobile devices provides a poor, disorienting user experience and hides critical CTAs (like the 'Details' button) off-screen.
findings.suggestion: Implement a responsive card-based layout for data tables on mobile viewports, stacking columns vertically for each vehicle row instead of using a rigid grid table.

findings.user_goal: Switch between primary application views using the mobile bottom tab bar.
findings.problem: The bottom navigation bar on mobile viewports extends beyond the screen width and does not adapt to the viewport size.
findings.evidence: On analytics.html and other mobile pages, the bottom navigation bar causes horizontal overflow (e.g., 528px wide on a 390px viewport). Items like 'Analytics', 'Alerts', and 'Settings' are cut off on the right edge.
findings.why_it_matters: Bottom tab bars should be fixed and fully visible. If items are pushed off-screen, users may not realize they exist or may struggle to swipe a fixed bottom bar to reach primary navigation links.
findings.suggestion: Limit the bottom tab bar to 4-5 core items, ensuring they distribute evenly within 100% of the viewport width (`width: 100vw; max-width: 100%`). Move secondary links into a 'More' menu.
findings.source_hint: Bottom navigation bar on mobile viewports

findings.user_goal: Filter vehicles by status (e.g., 'Maintenance' or 'Offline') to locate them on the map.
findings.problem: Status filters successfully update the bottom list drawer but fail to apply to the visual map markers.
findings.evidence: When clicking 'Offline' or 'Maintenance' on the index.html dashboard, the list updates to show only those 2 or 3 vehicles, but the map continues to display all 25 markers for all statuses.
findings.why_it_matters: This disconnect between the list state and the map visualization breaks user trust and creates confusion, as the map implies there are still active vehicles when the user specifically asked to only see offline ones.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the filtering logic applies globally to the page state, hiding map markers that do not match the currently selected status filter.

findings.user_goal: Access features like Drivers, Routes, Settings, or Maintenance.
findings.problem: Multiple prominent links in the primary navigation rail and bottom bar are unimplemented dead ends.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Drivers', 'Routes', 'Maintenance', and 'Settings' simply appends a '#' to the URL without navigating the user or providing any feedback that the feature is unavailable.
findings.why_it_matters: Presenting features that do not work frustrates users and makes the software feel broken or incomplete.
findings.suggestion: If these modules are not yet built, remove them from the navigation entirely, or implement a visual 'Coming Soon' state/toast notification when clicked.

findings.user_goal: Select a vehicle row or trigger its details on a mobile device.
findings.problem: Interactive elements on mobile are significantly smaller than touch accessibility standards.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings detect that table row checkboxes are 13x13px, the user profile icon is 36x36px, and the row 'Details' buttons are 58x26px. Mobile guidelines recommend at least 44x44px.
findings.why_it_matters: Small tap targets lead to accidental clicks and 'fat-finger' errors, increasing user friction on touch screens.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding and minimum height of interactive buttons, icons, and checkboxes on mobile viewports to ensure they meet the minimum 44x44px touch target area.

findings.user_goal: Use assistive technology to filter lists or switch organizations.
findings.problem: Critical form controls lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: The Organization switcher dropdown (ux-9) and the status/fleet dropdowns (ux-12, ux-13) are missing associated `<label>` tags or `aria-label` attributes.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users will not know the purpose of these dropdowns, severely impairing their ability to navigate fleets or filter data.
findings.suggestion: Add visually hidden `<label>` elements linked via `id` to the `<select>` inputs, or add descriptive `aria-label` attributes (e.g., `aria-label="Select Organization"`).
